entries.note: “Underwhelming” and what readers should have found surprising are evaluative judgments without a stated performance standard.

entries.test: The AAAI survey's questions, respondent population, and results would establish the reported finding; publicly demonstrated AGI achieved through scaling alone would refute the additional assertion that those doubts were correct.
entries.note: This combines a presently checkable survey report with an endorsement of scaling's ultimate insufficiency. The latter has no deadline.
This expresses caution and distinguishes media sentiment from investor sentiment. It specifies no concrete outcome or relationship whose occurrence would settle the whole claim.

entries.test: Public commentary and reporting from approximately August 2023 and August 2025 would show whether widespread portrayals shifted from treating Altman as a visionary authority to treating him as a deceptive promoter.
entries.note: The metaphors describe public reputation, making this more than a direct insult. “Many” does not require a majority.
There is no shared operational reading of simultaneously “drowning out” critics and “pouring good money after bad.” Those conditions leave the claimed impossibility without an agreed test.

entries.test: Public research publications and demonstrations would show new AI approaches emerging in response to documented shortcomings of existing approaches.
entries.note: The context gives “new approaches” a plain referent in AI research. The prediction is firm but has no deadline.
